title: Rav Chaviva bar Kohen
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Shekalim 4:6 in the version of the Jerusalem Talmud printed with the Babylonian Talmud (the supplied transcription has 4:3 [1]). In the Jerusalem Talmud the reading is “Rabbi Ba bar Kohen asked Rabbi Yose a question.” Hyman suggests that “Rabbi Ba” was written and became “Chaviva.”

notes.text: The supplied footnote marker [1] has no supplied footnote text; that missing material remains held. The Guggenheimer digital Shekalim 4:3 has Rabbi Ba bar Kohen asking Rabbi Yose. The proposed רבי בא to חביבא development is Hyman’s conjecture, not a proved letter history.

The printed notice (Hyman, vol. I, p. 408) has 4:6 and carries no footnote marker. The supplied [1] is retained as a feature of the transcription. The main column of the inspected Shekalim 11b scan has Rabbi Ba bar Kohen, as does Guggenheimer’s digital Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 4:3. The margin marked Nusach haBavli reads Chaviva bar Kohen. The two readings are attested. Hyman’s account of how one arose from the other remains a conjecture.
